index.privacy.h: Your face never leaves this Mac.
index.privacy.local.d: Face data is encrypted with a Secure Enclave key and never uploaded.
index.privacy.keychain.d: Your login password goes into the Keychain, only after you sign the consent.
index.privacy.thresholds.d: Match and liveness thresholds are adjustable, and you can test them first.
index.privacy.honest.d: No depth camera on a MacBook. FaceTime camera plus a liveness model, with Touch ID or password as fallback.
index.buy.body: Face unlock, App Lock, now playing, AirPods, fill light, Labs and Control Center controls. Pay once, no subscription. The source is MIT licensed; getting it gives you the ready-to-run app.
index.buy.req: macOS 14+ · MacBook with a notch · Control Center controls need macOS 26
index.faq.faceid.a: No. A MacBook has no depth camera, so Andeville uses the FaceTime camera and an on-device liveness model. Touch ID and your password stay as the fallback.
index.faq.photo.q: Can a photo of me unlock my Mac?
index.faq.photo.a: The liveness model is there to reject photos and screens. You can raise the match and liveness thresholds in settings.
index.faq.password.q: Why does it need my login password?
index.faq.password.a: macOS unlocks with your password, so Andeville enters it once it recognizes you. It is kept in the Keychain, only after you sign the consent.
index.faq.notch.q: Does it work without a notch?
index.faq.notch.a: No. It needs a MacBook with a notch and macOS 14 or later.
index.faq.labs.a: Experiments you switch on in settings: presence sensing with an 18–22 kHz ultrasonic echo or your AirPods signal, and the desk browser.

help.title: Help · Andeville
help.head.title: Common questions
help.head.sub: Setting it up, using it, and fixing it.
help.start.title: Getting started
help.start.need.a1: A MacBook with a notch and macOS 14 or later. Control Center in the notch needs macOS 26.
help.start.setup.q: How do I set it up?
help.start.setup.a1: Open Andeville and its settings, then:
help.start.setup.a2: Allow the camera. Register your face, alone and in good light. Turn on lock screen unlock and enter your Mac password. Allow Accessibility so it can type that password for you.
help.start.setup.a3: Turn on “start at login” if you want it always running.
help.start.password.a1: In your Mac’s Keychain, only after you sign the consent. Your face data is encrypted and stays on this Mac.
help.daily.title: Every day
help.daily.unlock.q: How do I unlock my Mac?
help.daily.unlock.a1: At the lock screen, move the cursor onto the notch. If it doesn’t know you, use Touch ID or your password.
help.daily.applock.q: How do I lock an app?
help.daily.applock.a1: Add it to App Lock in settings. It checks your face each time it opens. Taking it off the list needs your face too.
help.daily.skip.q: How do I skip a track?
help.daily.skip.a1: Swipe with two fingers on the notch.
help.daily.airpods.a1: In the notch, as soon as they connect, with the battery for each bud and the case.
help.daily.control_center.q: How do I open Control Center?
help.daily.control_center.a1: Rest the cursor on the notch. You can set how fast it opens and closes. Needs macOS 26.
help.tune.title: Making it stricter
help.tune.wrong_face.q: It lets the wrong face in. What do I change?
help.tune.wrong_face.a1: Lower the match threshold, or raise the liveness threshold. Stricter settings may ask you to try again more often.
help.tune.dark.q: It can’t see me in the dark.
help.tune.dark.a1: Turn on screen light. The screen glows white while it looks.
help.tune.stay_ready.q: Can it stay ready at the lock screen?
help.tune.stay_ready.a1: Turn on stay awake. Closing the lid still puts the Mac to sleep.
help.labs.title: Labs
help.labs.presence.a1: It starts looking for you when you come back to your desk. It listens for an echo of a tone too high to hear, or watches your AirPods’ signal. Nothing is recorded.
help.labs.desk_browser.a1: Show the desktop and it becomes a browser behind your windows. ⌘D adds a bookmark.
help.fixes.title: If something doesn’t work
help.fixes.no_face.a1: Check camera access in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Camera, then register your face again.
help.fixes.no_unlock.q: It knows me but won’t unlock.
help.fixes.no_unlock.a1: Allow Accessibility in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility, and check you signed the Keychain consent.
help.fixes.update.a1: Install the new Andeville DMG over the old one.
help.fixes.face_id.a1: No. It uses the FaceTime camera and an on-device check for photos. Touch ID and your password always work.
help.end.title: Still have a question?

policy.title: Policy · Andeville
policy.app.face.p1: Stored on this Mac only, and never sent anywhere.
policy.app.face.p2: When you register your face, Andeville keeps the face data encrypted with a key held in the Secure Enclave.
policy.app.camera.p1: Used only while Andeville is checking for your face.
policy.app.camera.p2: That is when you register, at the lock screen, and when you open a locked app.
policy.app.password.p1: Kept in the macOS Keychain, and only after you sign the consent.
policy.app.password.p2: Andeville has to enter your login password to unlock your Mac, so it needs to hold it somewhere safe.
policy.app.presence.p2: In ultrasonic mode the speakers play a tone too high to hear and Andeville listens for the echo to tell whether someone is at the desk. In AirPods mode it reads the Bluetooth signal strength of your connected AirPods.
policy.app.desk.p1: Importing needs Full Disk Access, which you grant yourself.
policy.app.desk.p2: You turn it on in System Settings and can take it back at any time.
policy.app.limits.p2: A MacBook has no depth camera, so a very similar face, or a photo or video, may unlock it. A liveness check is there to turn those away, and Touch ID and your password always remain as the fallback.
policy.site.cookies.p1: One cookie, and only if you sign in.
policy.site.cookies.p2: Signing in to your account sets a single session cookie that keeps you signed in for up to 30 days. There is no analytics and no advertising, and the font is served from the site itself. The only third-party script is Google’s sign-in button, loaded on the Account page while you are signed out.
policy.site.account.p1: We keep what Google gives us to know it is you, and your licence.
policy.site.account.p2: Sign-in is with Google. We store your Google account’s ID, name, email address and picture link, and the licence key added to the account. We do not get your Google password. Deleting your account on the Account page removes that profile from our side; your licence key keeps working.
policy.site.links.p1: Other sites have their own policies.
policy.site.links.p2: Links to GitHub, the G.gear service site and regiontype.com take you off this site.
policy.site.email.p1: We use what you send only to reply.
policy.site.email.p2: If you write to us, we get your email address and whatever is in your message.
policy.buying.payment.p1: Orders are processed by Paddle.com, our reseller and Merchant of Record, which handles payment, sales tax and receipts. Paddle collects your name, email, country and payment details to complete the order; we never see your card.
policy.buying.refunds.p1: If Andeville isn’t right for you, ask for a refund within 14 days of purchase and you get your money back in full. Write to us from the Contact page or reply to your Paddle receipt.
policy.buying.licence.p1: A personal licence for one Mac. To move it to another Mac, write to us from the Contact page.
policy.buying.licence.p2: The source code is MIT licensed and public; getting it gives you the ready-to-run app.
policy.buying.download.p2: After paying you are taken to the Account page. Sign in with Google there and the licence is added to your account, with the download beside it.
policy.terms.who.p1: Andeville is made and run by g.gear service, in Seoul.
policy.terms.who.p2: These terms cover the Andeville app, this website and your account on it. By buying, downloading or using Andeville you agree to them.
policy.terms.buying.p2: Paddle.com is the reseller and Merchant of Record for every order, so Paddle’s own buyer terms apply to the payment, along with the price and refund terms above.
policy.terms.licence.p2: A personal licence lets you install and use Andeville on one Mac that you own or control. Don’t share, resell or publish your licence key or your download. A licence that is refunded or charged back stops working.
policy.terms.account.p2: You are responsible for what happens under your account. We may close an account, or turn off a licence, that is used to share keys or downloads or to break these terms.
policy.terms.warranty.p1: Andeville is provided as it is.
policy.terms.warranty.p2: Face unlock is a convenience, not a security guarantee: see “The limits” above. To the extent the law allows, g.gear service is not liable for loss or damage that comes from using Andeville, and our total liability is limited to what you paid for it. Nothing here takes away rights the law gives you as a consumer.
policy.terms.changes.p2: The date at the top changes when we do. If you keep using Andeville after a change, the new terms apply.
policy.changes.when.p1: The date at the top changes with it.
